definitions.explanation: Noun formed from {速|はや}い (fast), referring to how fast something moves or happens. Also used for speed as a magnitude in everyday and scientific contexts.

examples.japanese: {車|くるま}の{速|はや}さに{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was surprised by the car's speed.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}の{速|はや}さでは、{彼女|かのじょ}に{誰|だれ}もかなわない。
examples.english: When it comes to how fast she works, no one can match her.

notes:
Formed from the i-adjective {速|はや}い + さ (a suffix that turns adjectives into nouns expressing degree). Refers to the rate of motion or how quickly something is done.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {音|おと}の{速|はや}さ: the speed of sound
- {速|はや}さを{増|ま}す: to increase speed
- {目|め}にも{留|と}まらぬ{速|はや}さ: dizzying speed (lit. too fast for the eye to catch)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {速度|そくど}: speed, velocity — more technical and measured (e.g. km/h); {速|はや}さ is the everyday word
- {早|はや}さ: earliness — same reading but written {早|はや}, about timing (being early) rather than rate of motion
